title: Rapid semi-automatic segmentation of the spinal cord from magnetic resonance images: application in multiple sclerosis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Rapid semi-automatic segmentation of the spinal cord from magnetic resonance images: application in multiple sclerosis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】A new semi-automatic method for segmenting the spinal cord from MR images is presented.

evidence.text: A new semi-automatic method for segmenting the spinal cord from MR images is presented.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Rapid semi-automatic segmentation of the spinal cord from magnetic resonance images: application in multiple sclerosis》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】Using 3-D acquired T(1)-weighted images of the cervical spine from human controls and patients with multiple sclerosis, the intra- and inter-observer reproducibilities were evaluated, and compared favorably with an existing cord segmentation method.

evidence.text: Using 3-D acquired T(1)-weighted images of the cervical spine from human controls and patients with multiple sclerosis, the intra- and inter-observer reproducibilities were evaluated, and compared favorably with an existing cord segmentation method.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Rapid semi-automatic segmentation of the spinal cord from magnetic resonance images: application in multiple sclerosis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】Since the cord center-line is an intrinsic parameter extracted as part of the segmentation process, the image can be resampled such that the center-line forms one coordinate axis of a new image, allowing simple visualization of the cord structure and pathology; this could find wider application in standard radiological practice.

evidence.text: Since the cord center-line is an intrinsic parameter extracted as part of the segmentation process, the image can be resampled such that the center-line forms one coordinate axis of a new image, allowing simple visualization of the cord structure and pathology; this could find wider application in standard radiological practice.
